facts: Honey never spoils; edible pots of honey thousands of years old have been found in ancient Egyptian tombs, still perfectly good to eat thanks to its unique chemical makeup.
Bananas are naturally radioactive because they contain high levels of potassium-40, though you would need to eat millions of them at once to experience radiation poisoning.
Nutmeg is a potent hallucinogen if ingested in large quantities, containing a natural organic compound called myristicin that can cause severe dizziness, nausea, and psychedelic trips.
Carrots were originally purple or yellow; the iconic orange carrot was selectively bred by Dutch growers in the 17th century to honor William of Orange.
White and black chocolate come from the same cacao bean, but white chocolate contains only cocoa butter, sugar, and milk solids without any cocoa solids.
Peanuts are not actually nuts; they are legumes that grow underground, closely related to beans, lentils, and peas.
Pineapples take nearly three years to grow from a single plant to a fully harvested fruit, and each plant typically produces only one pineapple at a time.
Strawberries are the only fruit in the world that wear their seeds on the outside, with an average of 200 tiny seeds dotting the surface of each berry.
Apples float in water because 25 percent of their volume is made up entirely of trapped air pockets.
Avocados are classified botanically as single-seeded berries, and their fat content is predominantly heart-healthy monounsaturated fat.
Vanilla is the second most expensive spice in the world after saffron because every single orchid flower must be hand-pollinated manually with a tiny needle.
Ketchup was originally sold in the 1830s as a medicinal cure for indigestion, diarrhea, and jaundice before it was ever used as a condiment.
Watermelons can be grown in square shapes in Japan by placing the young fruit inside heavy glass or metal cube boxes as they grow on the vine.
Almonds are not true nuts either; they are hard seeds enclosed within a stony fruit shell produced by a deciduous tree related to peaches and plums.
Popcorn is the oldest snack food known to humanity, with archaeologists discovering fossilized popcorn kernels in caves in New Mexico dating back over 5,000 years.

Baking soda and baking powder are entirely different chemical agents; baking soda requires an acid to activate, while baking powder already contains its own powdered acid.
